claim: Pure Malbolge stored-program control flow with in-memory relational equality comparison (CMP_EQ) for seven fixed 11-byte shapes. The opcode and the operands/branches that are emitted are loaded from RAM. JMP (0x0C) emits prog_6. JZ (0x01, condition in prog_1) emits prog_8 when 0 and prog_7 when 1. CALL (0x0E) emits prog_8 then prog_4. CMP_EQ (0x04) compares prog_1 against prog_4 in memory, emitting prog_8 (0x42) when 1==1 and prog_7 (0x43) when 1!=2. Same binary, both engines, matching step counts, strictly under the 59049 limit.
scope: These seven shapes only. The JMP immediate is read from RAM; JZ distinguishes condition 0 from 1; CALL is one frame deep; CMP_EQ compares equality with in-memory operand 1 and operand 2. Not a general program counter and not arbitrary MBIR.

cases.name: JMP skip HALT
cases.description: Opcode 0x0C emits prog_6 (0x41). The target byte is not classified.

cases.name: JMP other immediate
cases.description: Same path with prog_6 = 0x58, so the emitted byte is the one loaded from RAM.

cases.name: CALL then return
cases.description: Opcode 0x0E emits prog_8 (0x42) and then prog_4 (0x41).

cases.name: CMP_EQ taken (1==1)
cases.description: Opcode 0x04 with prog_1 == 1 and prog_4 == 1. Branch taken, emits prog_8 (0x42).

cases.name: CMP_EQ not taken (1!=2)
cases.description: Opcode 0x04 with prog_1 == 1 and prog_4 == 2. Branch not taken, emits prog_7 (0x43).

not_demonstrated: A general program counter that fetches arbitrary MBIR in a cycle.
Using the JMP target as an arbitrary runtime selector (landing on HALT is not in this image).
CMP_EQ with arbitrary width or multi-trit comparison operands beyond the demonstrated relational domain.
A call stack deeper than one frame.
